- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
h14.

**Computation site**

The derived metadata is computed by `RebuildMemoPayload` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`, which delegates to the goldmark markdown service's `ExtractAll` method in `internal/markdown/markdown.go:356` (a single AST walk). The result is stored on `memo.Payload.Property` (and `memo.Payload.Tags`). A standalone `ExtractProperties` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:193`) does the same property extraction. These stored properties are surfaced to the API by `convertMemoPropertyFromStore` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:315`.

**Triggers (recomputation)**

- **Create memo** — `CreateMemo` calls `RebuildMemoPayload` before persisting (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`).
- **Update memo** — `UpdateMemo` calls `RebuildMemoPayload`, but only when the `content` field is in the update mask (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`, inside the `if path == "content"` branch at line 436).
- **Batch backfill runner** — `Runner.RunOnce` re-runs `RebuildMemoPayload` over all memos in batches and writes back the payload (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27`, calling at line 52).

**Extracted properties**

The walk over the parsed markdown AST extracts (`storepb.MemoPayload_Property`):
- `Title` — text of the first block-level child if it's an H1 heading (`markdown.go:387`).
- `HasLink` — true if any link node is present (`KindLink`, line 394).
- `HasCode` — true if any code block / fenced code block / inline code span is present (line 397).
- `HasTaskList` — true if any task checkbox is present (`KindTaskCheckBox`, line 400).
- `HasIncompleteTasks` — true if any task checkbox is unchecked (line 403).

(`ExtractAll` also derives `Tags` and `Mentions` from the same walk, stored on the payload alongside `Property`.)

## Summary

The derived memo metadata is computed in two related layers: a persisted **Payload.Property** (rebuilt on write) and a per-request **Snippet** (computed at read/convert time).

### 1. Where the computation happens

**Persisted properties/tags — rebuilt on write:**
- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74` — `RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, markdownService)`. This is the entry point. It calls `markdownService.ExtractAll(memo.Content)` and assigns the results:
  ```go
  data, err := markdownService.ExtractAll([]byte(memo.Content))
  ...
  memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
  memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
  ```

**Actual markdown parsing / extraction:**
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:356` — `func (s *service) ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)`. This is the single-pass goldmark AST walk that computes everything (lines 371–411 quoted below). There is also a standalone `ExtractProperties` at `markdown.go:193` (same logic, not used by the rebuild path).

**Snippet (not stored in payload — generated on demand):**
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:264` — `GenerateSnippet(content, maxLength)`.
- Called via `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:83` `getMemoContentSnippet`, which is invoked during conversion at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:76` (`memoMessage.Snippet = snippet`) and for related-memo previews at converter lines 225/248.

### 2. Which operations trigger recomputation

`RebuildMemoPayload` is called from three places:
- **CreateMemo** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`
- **UpdateMemo** (only when the `content` field is in the update mask) — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`
- **Batch backfill runner** — `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52` inside `RunOnce`, which rebuilds the payload for all memos in batches of 100 and persists via `Store.UpdateMemo`.

The **Snippet** is recomputed on every read/convert (not persisted).

### 3. What the computation extracts

From `ExtractAll` (`markdown.go:371–411`), stored in `memo.Payload`:
- **Tags** (`[]string`) — from `#tag` nodes, deduplicated preserving case (`markdown.go:377, 418`).
- **Property** (`storepb.MemoPayload_Property`):
  - `Title` — text of the document's first block if it is an H1 heading (`markdown.go:384–388`)
  - `HasLink` — any `KindLink` node (`markdown.go:394`)
  - `HasCode` — any `KindCodeBlock`, `KindFencedCodeBlock`, or `KindCodeSpan` (`markdown.go:397`)
  - `HasTaskList` — any `TaskCheckBox` node (`markdown.go:400`)
  - `HasIncompleteTasks` — a task checkbox that is unchecked (`markdown.go:402–403`)

The `Property` proto fields are defined at `/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/memo.pb.go:85` (`HasLink`, `HasTaskList`, `HasCode`, `HasIncompleteTasks`, `Title`).

Note: `ExtractAll` also collects `Mentions` (`@username`) into `ExtractedData`, but the rebuild path only persists `Tags` and `Property` — mentions are used elsewhere. The **Snippet** is a separate plain-text summary (max 64 chars via `GenerateSnippet`, `memo_service_webhooks.go:85`) and is not part of the stored payload.

Store-side struct for the extraction result: `ExtractedData` at `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:21`.</result>
